en: Maybe you should go home, then. Then you can goof off all you want.
Yeah, but one time my phone ran out of juice mid-shift and when I asked the manager if I could go home, they wouldn't let me! Isn't that harsh?
That is. A club this size should still be able to get by with one person missing.
Right! I wish you were the manager, Kiryu-san.
If I were the manager, I don't know if I'd hire you to begin with.
That's not harsh. What did you expect them to say?
What? Maybe you should try harder to understand where a girl like me is coming from.
I think you have that backwards.
Do you live near your work, Kiryu-san?
Yeah. It's close enough that I can walk to it.
That's nice. It takes me an hour by train to get here from my house. It's a real pain in the butt if I'm tired.
An hour is a long time. It's probably even longer if you consider time spent waiting and changing trains. You must get tired doing that every day.
Yeah, for real. If I worked closer to home, I could spend all that commuting time doing other things instead.
You should move. It'd be a good opportunity to get out of your parents' house.
True, true. But rent around here is so ridiculously expensive. I'd rather stay home so I can save more money.
Yeah, even a studio apartment in Tokyo can cost a lot. Plus, it might not be safe for a girl to live on her own. Maybe staying home is better after all.
There are problems living close to work, too. Since you don't need to worry about your time commuting, you'll start running late more often.
Yeah, I'm totally that type. My university was right near my house, and I was almost always late for lectures.
My friend who commuted from two hours away would get pissed! She was all like, "How can you be late when you live so close!?" Hahah.
That's probably not something you should brag about.
Well, all things considered, it sounds like I'd be better off quitting my job and looking for other options.
Quite possibly. It all depends on what you think is more valuable⑬ your money or your time.
What? You really think I should quit? Do you not care about me at all, Kiryu-san?
I thought you were asking for real advice. It's about what you want, not what I want.
So then you're not just going to go along with me and my random griping?
Is that all it is? You shouldn't complain to your customers, you know.
Yeah, you're right. I'll try to watch it.
You don't seem terribly apologetic.
Of course not. I took it as a sign that you trusted me to really hear you out, and I was happy for that.
Ahaha! Nice save, mister. Sure, let's go with that, then!
You have to tough it out. Some days I have to drive passengers out pretty far, and then I wind up getting home late myself.
But I also wind up getting pretty big fares for those trips, so I think of the extra time as being a chance to get more money.
Oh, I see! So, is that why a hostess's salary is so much higher than a normal part-time job?
I think I get it now!
Hey, whatever makes sense to you.
You should work closer to home. It'd be way more cost-effective than moving closer to here.
No, that's no good at all. If my friends came in and saw me working, it'd be super weird.
Hm. I guess there are downsides to working near where you live, too.
That's why I try to work as far from home as I can. And given my occupation, I consider it just a consequence of the job.
Right. That's tough.
One hour isn't so bad. At least in the morning the trains are empty and you can get a seat.
Oh, but if I sit on a train, I'll fall asleep. That's why I make sure to stand.
That's a healthy attitude. If you stand aboard trains, it'll help tone your legs and hips. I think there are toning exercises like that.
Wow, really? I didn't know that! I'll definitely make sure to keep standing!
Why not get some sleep? It'll keep you from getting so tired at work.
Oh, no can do! Once I fall asleep, I have one heck of a time waking back up.
You don't wake up when you arrive at your station?
Nope! And setting an alarm won't work either.
The way the train rocks feels so good, it just lulls me right into a deep, deep sleep.
And since it's one big loop, the conductor never wakes me up at the end of the line. It's like Hotel Yamanote. It can be pretty handy actually!
That sounds nice. Plus, at this time of year, the insides of the trains are all heated.
I know, right!? It's far more economical than staying home. I can just ride for hours and hours!
I feel like we've lost the plot here.
But then you'd be a nuisance. You should pay for the time you spend riding.
What? But how?
How? Well... That's actually a good point.
See? You have to pay through those automated ticket machines, and they don't care how long you ride!
Hm. Still doesn't sound right to me.
Have someone drive you. Then you can head right home and get some good, proper sleep.
Hmm. There's the company car, but that's expensive. I'd really rather go home by myself than have to ask for the car.
Only girls who work a few days out of the week but earn a lot of money use the company car. If I used it every day, I wouldn't make any money.
I see. That's not very helpful, then.
Kiryu-san, do you prefer coffee or tea?
Coffee. I drink it during break at work all the time.
I guess I prefer it when I'm working too. It's definitely good when I'm tired.
Do you normally prefer tea then?
Tea. If I order a cake or something like that at a café, I think tea pairs with it better.
Oh, I wasn't expecting that!
Really? Men drink tea too, you know.
Yeah, but us girls can hang out over tea and chat for hours on end. Most guys can't handle spending time like that.
I guess tea does have a more feminine vibe associated with it. At least more than it does with men.
Well, I love tea, myself! I drink about ten cups a day!
Wow. You must be a real tea connoisseur.
Definitely! I even go to classes to brush up on my tea know-how!
Classes for tea? What do they teach?
Stuff like how to brew the perfect cup. Don't use a metal teapot, get it steeping as soon as the water's boiled. That sort of thing.
Interesting. I should give that a try sometime.
See? This is the sort of stuff I want to learn so I can put on a real classy tea party! You should try it, too, Kiryu-san! It'll be loads of fun!
Might be nice. Being able to serve guests tea as master of the house seems quite dignified.
I think it's usually the lady of the house who handles that, not the man.
Well, getting the place settings and stuff ready would be a hassle. Maybe I'll just do it once.
I'll stick with drinking it. That's good enough for me.
Then why don't you study up on the tea you're drinking? Different kinds have good and bad characteristics about them, along with a variety of flavors and prices.
Plus, some teas have certain effects, and others are good to drink at certain times. There are all sorts of neat trivia that's worth knowing!
Wow, I guess there's a lot to know. Maybe it is worth learning about.
I have nobody to invite. If we were talking liquor, that might be a different story. But I don't know if my friends are into tea.
All the more reason to invite them! It'd be a good chance for people who don't normally drink tea to really enjoy it!
Hm. But if I asked them, they might actually show up.
Sounds like a pain. What does it matter so long as it tastes good?
Everything matters! Even a slight difference in brewing can change the flavor completely!
Really? Maybe I should try to be more aware of the taste from now on.
Yes! It makes all the difference! A really good tea has to be brewed just right.
You really know your stuff, don't you?
Just relax and enjoy it. If you fuss too much over details, then a fun tea time just turns into a chore.
I'd rather not have tea at all than have tea that tastes all nasty and gross!
If you're taking a girl out for tea, Kiryu-san, you'd better be careful that you don't take her someplace that's subpar.
That's way too much. Is that even safe to do?
Well, it is full of tannins, so sometimes I get a bit anemic.
You sure know your stuff.
It's because I go to tea classes!
Whoa, hey now. I've never heard of tea making you anemic. Don't you think that's bad?
It's the same with coffee and green tea. Drinking too much tea has been linked with iron deficiencies.
Really? Then drinking too much coffee isn't good for you, either.
Then don't drink too much. Just drink as much as feels right and you'll be fine!
Ten cups is still way too much, I think.
I don't own very many clothes, you know.
Really? You strike me as very fashionable.
Nope! I own the bare minimum of what I need. I'd be in big trouble if I got careless and had nothing to wear because I forgot to wash them!
I don't have a lot of clothes, either. I don't dress well at home, and I've got my one good outfit for when I need to go out.
See? More people are like that than you'd think. Even fashionable folks wear the same things over and over, if you stop and pay attention.
If I had nice clothes, I'd want to wear them a lot, too. People who always buy new things to wear are wasting their money in my book.
Don't get lazy. People pay more attention to that sort of thing than you'd think. If you try to cut corners, people will notice.
That's why I try to make sure I look different each time.
When I go clothes shopping, I make it a point to buy things I can wear multiple ways.
You've put a lot of thought into this.
Maybe I could buy you some things. Perhaps an outfit or two that you'd like.
I really appreciate the offer, but...
My room's tiny and doesn't have a closet, so I don't have much room for clothes. That's why I try not to buy so much stuff.
Ah, so that's why.
This job requires a dress, so I can manage it. But I'd never be able to see my clients in my normal street clothes.
I have to wear a uniform for work, too. It's nice to not have to worry about fashion.
Right!? Even if I was given a choice to wear my street clothes, I would never do it.
I'd actually like to see that.
Plus, if I were to ever put on weight, none of my clothes would fit anymore! So I try my very hardest to maintain my figure.
That's good. Most people only notice they've gotten fat when it's too late. It's great to manage your weight proactively.
Yep! Not having to spend money on clothes is a big incentive!
Good point. So having a small amount of clothing isn't necessarily a bad thing after all. I'll try to keep that in mind myself.
I'd own more if I could though! My financial situation is my big limiting factor.
You can put that money to use towards other interests.
It's not about money. Even if you don't have many clothes, they can still be nice ones.
But isn't that kind of lame? You know, like buying stuff solely based on branding.
Besides, I think it shows more fashion sense if you can look good with clothes that cost less.
I see. It's not about what you wear, but how you wear it.
Is that your big worry? I thought dieting was about being concerned with your appearance, and whether your clothes fit was a secondary thing.
No, not at all! This one time I was trying to put on a pair of jeans and the zipper wouldn't go up all the way. I was mortified!
So now I go with one-size-fits-all dresses and gravitate towards loose-fitting clothes.
I see. Is that why loose clothing is in vogue nowadays?
Not everyone is concerned about how things fit around the waist.
But when I do have clothes like that, it's nice because I can wear them more than once.
Maybe I should look for some looser-fitting clothing myself.
That's no good. You'd stand out more if you wore things that were a tighter fit.
Well, that's not the way I want to stand out. Lots of girls wear extra layers of clothing so they don't have guys ogling them so much.
Really? That's kind of a shame.
Okay, Kiryu-san. Honest answer.
About what?
Have I put on weight recently?
Yeah. I feel like your face is a tiny bit fuller than when I first met you.
I thought as much. If someone else thinks that when looking at me, then it's probably true.
No, you don't look particularly different. I think you look like you normally do.
So you're saying I've been fat ever since you met me. I'm kind of offended.
I guess I'd better go on a diet, huh?
What do you normally eat?
Usually just one smallish meal a day.
